title: Fourier concentration from switching bounds
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$. Let $w$ be a positive integer and let $0<\varepsilon\le 1/2$. Suppose that for every integer $d\ge0$, the probability that a random restriction with each coordinate left free independently with probability $1/(10w)$ has decision-tree depth at least $d$ is at most $2^{-d}$, and the corresponding probability for free-coordinate probability $1/(20w)$ is at most $4^{-d}$. Then there is a finite family $\mathcal F$ of subsets of $[n]$ such that the total squared Fourier coefficient mass outside $\mathcal F$ is at most $\varepsilon$, and $|\mathcal F|\le 4\bigl(2(20w)^D\bigr)^2/\varepsilon$, where $D=30w\left\lceil\log_2(12/\varepsilon)\right\rceil$ (with the ceiling taken as a nonnegative integer).
